name: Nilotinib (CML, chronic phase, first-line)

biomarkers.note: CML is defined by the BCR::ABL1 fusion (Philadelphia chromosome); confirm Ph-positive or BCR::ABL1-positive by qPCR at diagnosis. A T315I kinase-domain mutation confers resistance to nilotinib (and to imatinib, dasatinib and bosutinib); ponatinib or asciminib is the treatment option for T315I. Per Standard Guidelines (NCCN), Chronic Myeloid Leukemia v2.2027.

lineOfTherapy: first-line for newly diagnosed chronic-phase CML (a second-generation TKI)

eligibilityCriteria.requirement: BCR::ABL1-positive (Ph-positive) chronic-phase CML confirmed by qPCR
eligibilityCriteria.locator: v2.2027, CML workup (Ph-positive or BCR::ABL1 positive by qPCR)

drugs.name: Nilotinib

provenance.locator: MS-27 (recommended starting dose of nilotinib is 300 mg twice daily for newly diagnosed CP-CML)

drugs.notes: Source: Standard Guidelines (NCCN), Chronic Myeloid Leukemia v2.2027, MS-27. Nilotinib 300 mg PO twice daily for newly diagnosed CP-CML (dosePerUnit 300 mg is the single-administration dose given twice daily; total 600 mg/day). Days 1 to 28 represents continuous daily dosing. Take on an empty stomach (no food 2 hours before and 1 hour after). Avoid coadministration with proton-pump inhibitors and H2 blockers. Continue until loss of response, progression or intolerance.

supportiveCare: Nilotinib prolongs the QT interval and carries a boxed warning for sudden death: obtain a baseline ECG, correct hypokalemia and hypomagnesemia before starting, repeat ECG about 7 days after initiation and periodically, and avoid concurrent QT-prolonging drugs and strong CYP3A4 inhibitors.
Administer on an empty stomach; avoid proton-pump inhibitors and H2 blockers (reduced absorption).
Monitor BCR::ABL1 (IS) by qPCR at milestones; if resistance, test for kinase-domain mutations (T315I directs ponatinib or asciminib).

monitoring: ECG/QTc at baseline, about 7 days after starting, and periodically; serum potassium and magnesium
CBC with differential at baseline and periodically
BCR::ABL1 (IS) by qPCR at approximately 3, 6 and 12 months and periodically thereafter (CML-G)
fasting glucose/lipids and vascular risk (nilotinib is associated with arterial occlusive events)

doseModificationRules.condition: QTc prolongation or grade 3 to 4 toxicity
doseModificationRules.text: Interrupt for QT prolongation or significant toxicity, correct electrolytes, and resume at a reduced dose per prescribing information. Physician decides.

guideline.locator: MS-27 (recommended starting dose of nilotinib is 300 mg twice daily for newly diagnosed CP-CML; 400 mg twice daily in later-line/resistant setting); PPI/H2 blocker avoidance (CML-D drug interactions); T315I/ponatinib option (manuscript and CML footnote)

provenanceNote: ONCQIS Standard Protocol draft for first-line nilotinib (a second-generation TKI) in chronic-phase, BCR::ABL1-positive CML. Dose grounded to Standard Guidelines (NCCN), Chronic Myeloid Leukemia v2.2027, MS-27: nilotinib 300 mg PO twice daily for newly diagnosed CP-CML. Modeled as continuous twice-daily oral therapy (cycleLengthDays 28 for reporting, cycles null, days 1 to 28 = continuous; dosePerUnit 300 mg per administration). QTc, electrolyte and vascular monitoring are emphasized because nilotinib prolongs QT (boxed warning) and is associated with arterial occlusive events. BCR::ABL1 is the diagnostic and monitoring biomarker; a T315I mutation directs ponatinib or asciminib. histology and treatmentIntent are VERIFY.
